title: Computation-Sublinear Refresh for Forward-Secure CGKA
statement_paraphrase: Does there exist an updatable distributed broadcast encryption scheme, hence a forward-secure CGKA protocol, whose refresh algorithms run in time sublinear in the group size (not merely producing succinct output), given the source already has a scheme with sublinear communication but polynomial-time refresh, and a separate scheme with fully sublinear complexity but no forward secrecy?

evidence.claim: Source (Bartusek, Bitansky, Dodis, Garg, Wu, ePrint 2026/1677) poses this directly on page 6 and as Remark 5.7.

The source's own second construction achieves full logarithmic complexity but explicitly without forward secrecy; this is progress on an easier sibling question, not a resolution of the stated open problem.

No independent resolution found; adjacent concurrent works (Auditable CGKA 2026/1710, BeeKEM 2026/1434, Updatable PKE variants) address related but distinct efficiency/audit questions, not this exact one.

queries_run: updatable distributed broadcast encryption sublinear refresh CGKA forward secrecy 2026
"CGKA" "logarithmic complexity" decomposed LWE post-compromise security not forward secure eprint 2026

G1_barrier.evidence: No named external barrier or transferred open problem asserted by the source.

G4_dual_use.evidence: A positive resolution is a constructive efficiency improvement, not an attack; a negative resolution yields no instantiable attack on deployed MLS/Signal-style systems.

P1.justification: Phrased and pursued as a pure existence/construction question; no impossibility direction is emphasized by the source.
P1.construction_side_dual: Design an updatable DBE whose refresh algorithms avoid touching all of S, e.g. via a tree-structured or incrementally-updatable key-encoding that still supports the forward-secrecy re-randomization guarantee.

P2.justification: The source's own second construction (logarithmic complexity, no forward secrecy) is a settled, easier sibling that isolates exactly the missing ingredient; a crisp generalization hypothesis follows directly from it.
P2.restriction_axis: presence of the forward-secrecy refresh requirement
P2.settled_base_case: source's log-complexity construction achieving PCS with no forward secrecy
P2.next_rung: add a forward-secrecy-providing refresh while keeping sublinear time
P2.generalization_hypothesis: Does the log-complexity (no-FS) construction's structure survive once a refresh operation providing forward secrecy is layered on top, or does FS's re-randomization requirement inherently force touching all of S?

P3.justification: Recombining two distinct technique lines from the same paper (the log-complexity PCS-only structure and the FS-providing refresh mechanism) is a real synthesis task with substantial ambient convention load from matrix commitments and decomposed LWE.
P3.candidate_technique: recombination of the source's two constructions (log-complexity aggregation structure + FS refresh mechanism)
P3.ambient_convention_load: high (matrix commitments, decomposed LWE, CGKA security games)

V1.justification: Existence question is precise as an existential over o(|S|)-time algorithms, adversary/corruption model inherited cleanly from the source's own definitions; the source does not pin down which model (ROM vs standard) the sought scheme should live in, and 'sublinear' names no specific target rate.
V1.idealization: unspecified for the open question itself (source's own constructions mix ROM and standard-model variants)
V1.vacuous_reading: A scheme whose refresh runs in time O(|S|/log|S|) or similarly trivially-sublinear-but-not-meaningfully-faster time would formally satisfy 'sublinear' without resolving the practical question.

V2.justification: Running time of a candidate algorithm is mechanically profileable, but full security (the actual crux) rests on computational hardness assumptions over large structures and is not finite-instance decidable the way the running-time predicate is.
V2.finite_instantiation: running-time profiling of a candidate refresh algorithm is checkable; security is not brute-force verifiable at small scale

V3.justification: CGKA/broadcast-encryption security games are within EasyCrypt's usual scope and a recombination-style decomposition is plausible to sketch, but no cheap machine-checkable witness short of the full construction exists.
V3.decomposition_cost: moderate, contingent on the recombination succeeding

O1.justification: CGKA/secure-group-messaging efficiency is an active, well-resourced subfield (MLS standardization, multiple concurrent 2026 works on adjacent questions found in Scout), so neither the provenance-as-aside nor the low-attention nor the narrow-subarea bonus applies.
O1.adjacent_solved_likelihood: moderate (adjacent efficiency questions are being actively solved by several groups)

O2.justification: Fully open-access source and bounded compute profile, but the likely proof, if a recombination succeeds, runs long given the machinery involved and lacks clean a priori lemma boundaries.

reasons: R4: 'sublinear' names no fixed rate, so a trivially-sublinear construction could satisfy the letter without the spirit of the question.

configuration.entry_rung_latex: Does there exist a succinct updatable DBE scheme whose UpdPK, UpdSK run in time sublinear in $|S|$?
configuration.leading_plan_class: Case Planner to attempt recombining the source's two constructions; Scout to check for the newest concurrent CGKA-efficiency work before committing; Refuter limited to profiling candidate running times, not security.
configuration.falsifiable_milestone: A candidate refresh algorithm with a clearly sublinear running-time profile on toy parameters, plus a sketched (not necessarily complete) security argument reduction to the source's existing assumptions.
configuration.yield_on_failure: A precise account of which structural feature of the forward-secrecy refresh forces touching all of S in every attempted recombination, as a candidate barrier note.
contract_fields_needing_human_input: target asymptotic rate for 'sublinear' (polylog vs merely o(|S|))
whether the sought scheme may use a random oracle
